text.p: Anglo-Austrlian mining group RTZ-CRA on Thursday reported what it called encouraging results from exploration, including work at its Canadian diamond operation.
The group said it has completed a review of the group's combined exploration. This has eliminated overlaps and cut back marginal programmes, with reductions spread evenly across the major regions.
Cost savings this year will be offset by one-off restructuring costs, the group said in its half-year results, but annual savings will be $50 million from 1997.

The company said most of the sample from its A-154 South diamond pipe in the North West Territories of Canada has been processed with encouraging results. The sample grade is 4.6 carats per tonne, with the largest gemstone found to date weighing 6.2 carats.

"The results support earlier indications of an inferred resource of 8.4 million tonnes down to 250 metres," it said, adding a valuation of $260 per tonne compared favourably with operating mines around the world.
Earlier in the year, a grade of 4.02 carats per tonne was indicated from another pipe, A-418, where mining of a bulk sample will be completed by the end of the year.
On copper and gold, RTZ-CRA said potential for "a significnat underground orebody" adjacent to the Grasberg mine in Indonesia has been indicated by drilling results.
It said the Las Cruces prospect in Andalucia, Spain, continues to return promising results.

RTZ-CRA added that it has contracts of work applications on "strategically well-sited land positions in Kalimantan, Indonesia, where there has been considerable exploration activity following the neighbouring discovery of a multi-million ounce gold deposit."
